subject: Post-call: Clarify inference evaluation pack + latency traces
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@clarityhealth.ai>, Caleb Tran <caleb.tran@clarityhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Clarify inference evaluation pack + latency traces

Hi Elena / Caleb —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Summary of needs we heard
- Primary: fast interactive summarization for clinician notes (95th pct latency target ~250ms).
- Secondary: nightly batch embeddings for search and similarity (throughput goal ~1.5k docs/hour).
- Constraints: PHI-safe processing inside VPC; SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

2) Recommended starting models (based on quality vs cost tradeoff we discussed):
- rdw-3.7-slim-q4f32 (likely best latency/cost for short clinical prompts)
- rdw-7b-instruct-int8 (higher quality, expect ~1.5x latency)
- rdw-2.1-embed-compact (embeddings for nightly jobs)

3) What we shared in the call (links & attachments)
- Attached: clarity-eval-pack-20260825.pdf — benchmark snapshots, prompt templates, and a simple regression checklist.
- Redwood-verified performance profiles (attached CSV + live link below) with TPS and p50/p95/p99 latency for each model on our hosted runtime.
- Drive folder with sample prompt sets and reproducible bench scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_test_benchmark_refs

4) Immediate next steps
- Action (Clarity): confirm scope (interactive only vs interactive + batch) by EOD Thurs so we can size pilot.
- Action (Redwood): we’ll seed a pilot config (1-week trial) with rdw-3.7-slim-q4f32 + telemetry hooks; Marissa will share perf traces and a proposed canary rollout plan.

If that matches your expectations I’ll open a HubSpot deal record and drop a pilot kickoff invite.

Thanks —
Priyom

Priyom — thanks, that’s helpful and accurate. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- We definitely need VPC/on-prem option for PHI; can you confirm the pilot can run inside our AWS account?
- The 250ms p95 target is aspirational — for MVP we can accept p95 up to 400ms but p99 should stay under 1s.
- We’ll start with interactive only for the pilot.

We’ll confirm scope by Thursday. Please go ahead and provision the pilot config so we can review traces.

—Elena
Elena Soto | Dir of Product, ClarifyHealth
elena.soto@clarityhealth.ai | +1 (617) 555-0192
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarify inference evaluation pack + latency traces

Elena / team — quick technical notes and traces I promised. Attached are two things: the one-page perf snapshot (clarity-eval-pack-20260825.pdf) and our Redwood-verified-profiles.csv with p50/p95/p99 numbers observed on hosted rdw clusters. Highlights: 

- rdw-3.7-slim-q4f32 on g4dn-like instance: p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 190ms, p99 ~ 420ms (single-request baseline, no batching).
- rdw-7b-instruct-int8 on a4-similar: p50 ~ 95ms, p95 ~ 380ms, p99 ~ 820ms (higher quality; plan for heavier mem footprint).
- Embedding model (rdw-2.1-embed-compact) throughput: ~2200 embeds/sec on batch size 256 (network overhead dependent on VPC egress).

Prompt set note — included sample prompts that mirror the clinician note length you mentioned; please flag any variations so we can re-run the microbench.

I also added a short regression checklist in the PDF: prompt-anchored evals, baseline seed inputs, and automated alert thresholds (e.g., p95 latency increase > 25% or generation-quality drop on BLEU/ROUGE proxies).

Attachment stubs:
- clarity-eval-pack-20260825.pdf (1.2 MB)
- redwood-verified-profiles.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min technical kickoff later this week to walk through the traces and the rollout plan.

—Marissa
